input.summary: I read the whole of `git diff 28a6065..HEAD`, ran the machinery suite (112 passed), `adss check` (18 PASS), ruff and sqlfluff (all clean), and queried the built warehouse read-only. The slice is correct for the model it ships and the acceptance data agrees exactly. What I found are latent defects in the new generic machinery: two edges to the same target entity (or a self-edge) generate a bridge whose duplicate key column DuckDB silently collapses with no error anywhere; `check_relationships` only validates the last mapping that declares a given edge id; `key_shape()` throws away function names, which are as load-bearing as the casts it exists to compare; and `dar generate` writes into `checks/` but never sweeps its own stale output, which the existing comment in `das unpack` already names as a hazard that aborts `adss check`. Nothing is blocking.

findings.finding: A second edge from one entity to the same target entity — or a self-edge — makes the stage CTE emit two columns with the same name, and DuckDB silently resolves the ambiguity instead of erroring, so one inherited key is dropped with nothing reporting it. ADR 0006's Consequences claim the opposite: "filtering on rel_name makes a second edge between the same two entities a new structure rather than a silent collision". The pair views are separated by rel_name; the bridge columns are not.
findings.evidence:
Both `_stage_cte` and `_branch` name an inherited key `model.entity(edge.target_entity_id).key_column`, which depends only on the target entity, never on the edge. Adding a second CHILD→PARENT edge to the neutral fixture model and calling `bridge_sql` produced:
```
occurred AS (
SELECT
    revision.child_key AS child_key,
...
    child_points_at_parent.parent_key AS parent_key,
    child_also_points_at_parent.parent_key AS parent_key,
```
and a self-edge (CHILD→CHILD) produced `revision.child_key AS child_key, ... child_follows_child.child_key AS child_key`. `formatted()` (sqlfluff, .sqlfluff config) accepted the duplicate-alias SQL — "sqlfluff ACCEPTED the duplicate-alias bridge; length 7577". DuckDB 1.5.5 then resolves it without error: `WITH s AS (SELECT a.k AS k, b.p AS p, d.p AS p FROM a LEFT JOIN b ... LEFT JOIN d ...) SELECT s.k, s.p FROM s AS s` returned `[(1, 20)]` (one of the two `p` values, silently) and `DESCRIBE` reported a single `p` column. Because `entity_keys`/`bridge_columns` dedupe by entity too, the built bridge matches its published contract and `adss check`'s first finding still passes; both edges' generated `__resolves` checks join on the one surviving column and both pass as well.
findings.fix: Refuse the model shape, or make the column name carry the edge. Cheapest: in `entity_ids`/`bridge_sql`, raise a `UssError` when `model.edges_from(e)` contains two edges with the same `target_entity_id`, or when `source_entity_id == target_entity_id`, naming ADR 0006 — the design is not decided for that case yet and a loud refusal is what ADR 0006 asks for ("a case the design cannot handle fails the build loudly rather than answering a question wrongly").

findings.finding: `check_relationships` keys its `loaded` map on the edge id, so when two mappings declare the same edge — an entity loaded from a second source, which blueprint B2 exists to make possible — only the last one in the sequence is validated. The earlier mapping's silent-skip violation passes unnoticed, which defeats the entire purpose of the check.
findings.evidence:
`loaded = {edge.id: (mapping, edge) for mapping in mappings for edge in mapping.relationships}` — a later entry overwrites an earlier one. Run against the repo's own fixtures:
```
broken child mapping alone                        -> refused: bad_relationship_table.yaml: M6 -- CHILD_POINTS_AT_PARENT names source_table 'das__staged....
two CHILD mappings, broken FIRST, good LAST       -> ACCEPTED (no MappingError)
two CHILD mappings, good FIRST, broken LAST       -> refused: bad_relationship_table.yaml: M6 -- ...
```
The order is whatever `sorted((ROOT / "dab" / "mappings").glob("*.yaml"))` yields (tests/test_relationship_rules.py:84), i.e. filename order. The same shape recurs at mapping.py:249, `target = next((one for one in mappings if one.entity_id == declared.target_entity_id), None)`, which consults only the first mapping for the target entity, so a second source's key expression is never compared against the target expression.
findings.fix: Iterate over `[(mapping, edge) for mapping in mappings for edge in mapping.relationships]` rather than collapsing to a dict, and check each declaration; use the dict only for the "declared but not loaded" membership test. At mapping.py:255 build `keys` from every mapping whose `entity_id` matches the target, not just the first.

findings.finding: `key_shape()` anonymises every identifier that is not a type keyword, and a function name is an identifier — so two expressions that produce demonstrably different VARCHARs compare as the same shape and M6 accepts the pair. This is the one mechanical guard against "pairs that join to nothing", and the docstring's own reasoning ("the casting may not differ, because a bare column and a cast produce different keys") applies to functions exactly as much as to casts.
findings.evidence:
```
'left(code, 5)'      vs 'right(code, 5)'      -> SAME SHAPE (passes M6)   '?(?, 5)' | '?(?, 5)'
'upper(customer_id)' vs 'lower(customer_id)'  -> SAME SHAPE (passes M6)   '?(?)' | '?(?)'
'ltrim(code)'        vs 'rtrim(code)'         -> SAME SHAPE (passes M6)   '?(?)' | '?(?)'
'md5(code)'          vs 'sha256(code)'        -> SAME SHAPE (passes M6)   '?(?)' | '?(?)'
```
(run against the real `adss.mapping.key_shape`). Nothing else catches it: `check_mapping`'s M2 clause only counts `primary_keys` entries — its own docstring at mapping.py:132-134 says the key-shape half is "review-only until there is a composite key to check" — and `target_transformation_expression` has no shape rule at all outside M6.
findings.fix: Treat an identifier immediately followed by `(` as part of the shape (keep it lower-cased) rather than replacing it with `?`, so a function name survives the same way a cast does. A one-line change to the `anonymous` callback plus a lookahead in `_IDENTIFIER`.

findings.finding: `dar generate` is now a second writer into `checks/`, but only `das unpack` sweeps that directory. Rename or remove a relationship in `dab/model.yaml`, run `adss dar generate` (the documented per-layer command), then `adss check`, and the stale check file is still executed and aborts the whole run with a traceback before a single finding is printed — precisely the hazard the sweep was installed for.
findings.evidence: `dar_generate` iterates only `everything` (the files it generates) and never globs `project.checks_sql`; the only `glob("*.sql")` + `unlink()` is in `das_unpack` at cli.py:183-191. `run_checks` executes every file it finds: `for path in sorted(project.checks_sql.glob("*.sql")): passed, detail = _zero(connection, path.read_text())` (checks.py:63-64), and a generated relationship check naming a view that no longer exists raises rather than returning a count — confirmed against the real warehouse: `SELECT 1 FROM dab."v_NOPE"` → `CatalogException: Catalog Error: Table with name v_NOPE does not exist!`. The comment that introduced the sweep says exactly this: "A renamed or removed contract would otherwise leave an orphan check behind, and an orphan check aborts the whole run before any finding is printed" (cli.py:146-147). `adss build` is safe only by accident of ordering (das_unpack runs before dar_generate, cli.py:326/330), and `adss dar generate --check` — the CI drift gate — does not report the stale file either; only `das unpack --check` does.
findings.fix: Give `dar_generate` the same sweep over `project.checks_sql` for the names `_generated_checks` produces (and over `project.dar_sql`), or move the whole sweep into one place both writers call.

findings.finding: The same anonymisation false-refuses a perfectly correct mapping in three cases, and the refusal message then blames the casting, which is not what differs. Conventions §1.1 makes this reachable: DAS column names are the source's own words, and a source is free to call a column `date` or `text`.
findings.evidence:
`_SHAPE_WORDS` holds `date`, `text`, `int`, `real`, `float`, `char`, `string`, `uuid`, `decimal`, `numeric`, `double`, `timestamp`, `boolean` — all plausible column names — so a column named after one is preserved verbatim while every other column becomes `?`:
```
'cast(text AS VARCHAR)' vs 'cast(note AS VARCHAR)' -> differs (refused)
      'cast(text as varchar)' | 'cast(? as varchar)'
'date'                  vs 'order_date'            -> differs (refused)   'date' | '?'
```
`_IDENTIFIER` is ASCII-only, so `key_shape('café')` is `'?é'` against `'?'` for any plain name; and a quoted identifier containing a space is split, `key_shape('"Order Id"')` → `'"? ?"'`. All three raise the M6 error at mapping.py:257-262, whose text says "the casting may not differ".
findings.fix: Extend `_IDENTIFIER` to `[^\W\d]\w*` (unicode-aware) and skip over double-quoted identifiers the same way literals are skipped. For the type-word collision, only treat a `_SHAPE_WORDS` match as shape when it is in type position (after `AS`) rather than anywhere.

findings.finding: The shot filename is now `question.id` with no validation, and nothing enforces that ids are unique or filename-safe. An id containing `/` or `..` escapes `.screenshots/`; an empty id falls back to `notebook.stem` AND passes `ADSS_QUESTION=""`, which the page reads as "show everything" — so that question's committed `answer.png`, the record of what was delivered, would silently be a picture of every question.
findings.evidence: `shot = into / f"{question or notebook.stem}.png"` (destination.py:100) with `question=question.id` (cli.py:348); `Question.id = str(front["id"])` in question.py:66 with no shape check, and `check_question` (question.py:86-141) never looks at the id. `destinations/app.py:43` is `only = os.environ.get("ADSS_QUESTION", "").strip()` and app.py:49 returns the element when `not only`, so an empty value renders all questions. Two questions sharing an id would also collide in `answers = {q.id: ...}` (app.py:105) and overwrite each other's shot. On the security half of this: the value itself is safe — `ADSS_QUESTION` goes into a list-form `subprocess.run(..., env=dict(os.environ, ...))` (destination.py:62-88, no `shell=True`) and reaches the page only as a string compared with `==`.
findings.fix: Validate the id where the question is read — a `[a-z0-9_-]+` pattern, non-empty, unique across `read_questions` — and raise `QuestionError` naming the file. That also protects the `answers` dict and the `_first_gap` reporting.

findings.finding: The page builds an answer for every question `read_questions` returns, including DRAFT and SUPERSEDED ones that `run_checks` deliberately skips, and it indexes `questions[1]` unconditionally. A draft question whose directory sorts first, or the removal of question 1, breaks the page for *every* question, so `adss shoot` fails for all of them rather than for the one that changed.
findings.evidence: `answers = {q.id: warehouse.execute(q.uss_sql).pl() for q in questions}` (app.py:105) has no status filter, while checks.py:119-129 skips DRAFT/SUPERSEDED with the reason "running either would fail the build on something nobody is answering". `q1 = questions[0]` (app.py:119) and `q2 = questions[1]` (app.py:222) are positional over `sorted(root.iterdir())` (question.py:81). The failure is loud — a raising cell makes `shoot` report "the page ran but cells failed" (destination.py:110-111) — which is why this is a note.
findings.fix: Have the page look questions up by id (or by status), not by position, and skip DRAFT/SUPERSEDED the way `run_checks` does. `adss shoot` (cli.py:343) should skip them too rather than writing an `answer.png` beside a question nobody is answering.

findings.finding: `das unpack` calls `_generated_checks(project)` for its dict keys alone, but that function reads `dab/model.yaml` and runs `formatted()` — the sqlfluff fixer — over every relationship check, then throws the SQL away. A DAS-only command now fails if the DAB model is unreadable or emits SQL sqlfluff rejects, and `das unpack --check` in CI pays for a formatter run whose output is discarded.
findings.evidence: cli.py:182 is `written_checks |= {project.checks_sql / name for name in _generated_checks(project)}` — iterating the dict yields only the file names. `_generated_checks` (cli.py:251-257) does `read_model(project.model)` and `formatted(sql, project.sqlfluff_config)` per check, and `formatted` re-raises anything sqlfluff throws as `SqlFormatError` (sqlformat.py:24-27). CI runs `uv run adss das unpack --check` after `dar generate --check` (.github/workflows/ci.yml).
findings.fix: Split the name computation from the SQL generation — e.g. have `das unpack` union in `relationship_checks(read_model(project.model)).keys()` directly and leave the formatting to `dar generate`.

findings.finding: `contracts_of()` has no callers anywhere in `src/`, `tests/` or `destinations/`, and its docstring — "Every contract this project declares. Used to generate the checks above." — is not true: the contract checks are generated in `cli.das_unpack` from `read_contract`, and the function sits directly above the new `relationship_checks`, whose own docstring says "The contracts generate the rest". Pre-existing rather than introduced by this slice, but the new neighbour makes the stale claim more confusing, not less.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "contracts_of" src tests destinations` returns exactly one line, the definition at checks.py:145. `git log -S "def contracts_of"` puts it in 3d2fa7e, before 28a6065, so it is not part of this diff.
findings.fix: Delete it, or call it from `cli.das_unpack` where the contract names are already being recomputed by a second `read_contract` pass.

checkedAndFound: Decimal vs float in the row-by-row acceptance compare: both halves of q02 cast to DECIMAL(28, 8) explicitly (docs/questions/02-.../staged.sql:7 and uss.sql:5), so both come back as Python Decimal and `_first_gap`'s tuple equality is exact, not lucky. Verified in DuckDB that the two sides sum to the same value: `Decimal('64942.69000000')` from `dar__uss._bridge` and from `das__staged.orders__current`.

No `eval`, `exec`, `shell=True`, `os.system`, `pickle` or `yaml.load` anywhere in src/, destinations/ or tests/ (grep). Both `subprocess.run` calls (engine.py:82, destination.py:62) are list-form with no shell. Nothing from outside the repository is interpolated into SQL, a path, a subprocess argument or an environment variable — every interpolated value comes from a committed YAML or Markdown file.

`ADSS_QUESTION`: traced from `question.id` through `cli.shoot_destination` → `shoot` → `_capture`'s env dict → `destinations/app.py:43`, where it is only `.strip()`ed and `==`-compared. It never reaches SQL, a shell, or a command argument. The only reachable harm is the filename, reported above.

`key_shape`'s literal-preserving loop against escaped quotes: `'it''s'` and `''''` survive verbatim, because the doubled quote is consumed as two adjacent literals covering exactly the same span, so parity is preserved and no identifier is swallowed. Empty and whitespace-only expressions return `''` without raising. A parameterised type survives intact — `cast(x AS DECIMAL(18, 4))` → `cast(? as decimal(18, 4))` — because digits are not identifiers.

The parentless child: `_inherit_cte` LEFT JOINs and partitions `row_number()` by the child key, so the single all-null row ranks 1 and the child keeps its row with a null inherited key, as ADR 0006 requires. The built bridge has 830 rows and 830 non-null `customer_key` against 830 orders, and 0 orders in `das__staged.orders__current` have a null `customer_id`.

Warehouse lock discipline (§9): `is_installed` opens read-only through `platform.reading`, whose `finally` closes the connection and decrements the `_open` counter before `dab_install` invokes the engine subprocess, so `require_detached` is not tripped and the new idempotence check does not break the one-writer rule.

No mutable default arguments introduced; `Model.relationships` and `Mapping.relationships` both default to `()`. `_first_gap` uses `zip(..., strict=False)` with an explicit length fallback, so unequal result lengths report rather than raise.

The bridge's published column contract was extended, not rearranged: `entity_keys` returns model order and CUSTOMER was appended after ORDER in dab/model.yaml (lines 17 and 63), so the built columns are `..., order_key, customer_key, _measure__...` — the slice-1 consumer contract is intact.

The `__one_target` check is stricter than the generator, never weaker: it ignores `ver_tmstp` and ignores the per-child `eff_tmstp <= _observed_at` window, so every tie the generator would silently resolve is flagged, and no tie the generator faces is missed. Both filter `row_st = 'Y'`.

The honesty caveat in docs/questions/README.md is factually right: `ship_country` equals the customer's `country` on all 830 orders (830 of 830 in DuckDB), and 0 bridge rows have an inherited customer whose country differs from the order's destination — so the claim that the answer alone does not prove the inheritance is accurate, not a hedge.

Tooling all green from a clean tree: `git status --porcelain` empty, `uv run pytest` 112 passed, `uv run adss check` 18 PASS / 0 FAIL, `uv run ruff check` clean, `uv run sqlfluff lint checks dar docs` clean.

findings.fix: Validate the id where the question is read — a `[a-z0-9_-]+` pattern, non-empty, unique across `read_questions` — and raise `QuestionError` naming the file. That also protects the `answers` dict and the `_first_gap` reporting.

findings.finding: The page builds an answer for every question `read_questions` returns, including DRAFT and SUPERSEDED ones that `run_checks` deliberately skips, and it indexes `questions[1]` unconditionally. A draft question whose directory sorts first, or the removal of question 1, breaks the page for *every* question, so `adss shoot` fails for all of them rather than for the one that changed.
findings.evidence: `answers = {q.id: warehouse.execute(q.uss_sql).pl() for q in questions}` (app.py:105) has no status filter, while checks.py:119-129 skips DRAFT/SUPERSEDED with the reason "running either would fail the build on something nobody is answering". `q1 = questions[0]` (app.py:119) and `q2 = questions[1]` (app.py:222) are positional over `sorted(root.iterdir())` (question.py:81). The failure is loud — a raising cell makes `shoot` report "the page ran but cells failed" (destination.py:110-111) — which is why this is a note.
findings.fix: Have the page look questions up by id (or by status), not by position, and skip DRAFT/SUPERSEDED the way `run_checks` does. `adss shoot` (cli.py:343) should skip them too rather than writing an `answer.png` beside a question nobody is answering.

findings.finding: `das unpack` calls `_generated_checks(project)` for its dict keys alone, but that function reads `dab/model.yaml` and runs `formatted()` — the sqlfluff fixer — over every relationship check, then throws the SQL away. A DAS-only command now fails if the DAB model is unreadable or emits SQL sqlfluff rejects, and `das unpack --check` in CI pays for a formatter run whose output is discarded.
findings.evidence: cli.py:182 is `written_checks |= {project.checks_sql / name for name in _generated_checks(project)}` — iterating the dict yields only the file names. `_generated_checks` (cli.py:251-257) does `read_model(project.model)` and `formatted(sql, project.sqlfluff_config)` per check, and `formatted` re-raises anything sqlfluff throws as `SqlFormatError` (sqlformat.py:24-27). CI runs `uv run adss das unpack --check` after `dar generate --check` (.github/workflows/ci.yml).
findings.fix: Split the name computation from the SQL generation — e.g. have `das unpack` union in `relationship_checks(read_model(project.model)).keys()` directly and leave the formatting to `dar generate`.

findings.finding: `contracts_of()` has no callers anywhere in `src/`, `tests/` or `destinations/`, and its docstring — "Every contract this project declares. Used to generate the checks above." — is not true: the contract checks are generated in `cli.das_unpack` from `read_contract`, and the function sits directly above the new `relationship_checks`, whose own docstring says "The contracts generate the rest". Pre-existing rather than introduced by this slice, but the new neighbour makes the stale claim more confusing, not less.

`key_shape`'s literal-preserving loop against escaped quotes: `'it''s'` and `''''` survive verbatim, because the doubled quote is consumed as two adjacent literals covering exactly the same span, so parity is preserved and no identifier is swallowed.
